verses.text: “Heaven’s Kingdom runs like this: a landowner went out early to hire workers for his vineyard.”
“He agreed to pay them a denarius for the day and sent them into his vineyard.”
“Around the third hour, he went out and saw more people standing idle in the marketplace.”
“He told them, ‘You go work in the vineyard too, and I’ll pay you whatever’s fair.’ So they went.”
“He went out again around the sixth and ninth hours and did the same.”
“Around the eleventh hour, he went out and found others still standing there. He asked, ‘Why have you been standing here all day with no work?’”
“They said, ‘Nobody hired us.’ He told them, ‘You go work in the vineyard too, and you’ll get what’s fair.’”
“When evening came, the vineyard owner told his manager, ‘Call the workers and pay them their wages, starting with the last and ending with the first.’”
“The workers hired around the eleventh hour came, and each got a denarius.”
“When the first workers came, they figured they’d get more. But each of them also got a denarius.”
“They took the money and started complaining about the landowner:”
“‘These last workers only did one hour, but you made them equal to us—we carried the whole day’s load in the blazing heat!’”
“He answered one of them, ‘Friend, I haven’t wronged you. Didn’t we agree on a denarius?”
“‘Take what’s yours and go. I choose to give this last worker the same as I gave you.”
“‘Can’t I do what I want with what belongs to me? Are you jealous because I’m generous?’”
“So the last will be first, and the first last. Many are invited, but few are chosen.”
As Jesus was heading up to Jerusalem, he pulled the twelve disciples aside and told them on the way:
“We’re going up to Jerusalem. The Son of Man will be handed over to the chief priests and teachers of the Law, and they’ll sentence him to death.”
“They’ll hand him over to the nations to be mocked, whipped, and crucified. On the third day, he’ll be raised.”
Then the mother of Zebedee’s sons came to Jesus with her sons. She knelt and asked him for something.
He asked her, “What do you want?” She said, “Promise that these two sons of mine will sit beside you in your Kingdom—one on your right, one on your left.”
Jesus answered, “You don’t know what you’re asking. Can you drink the cup I’m about to drink, and go through the baptism I’m about to go through?” They said, “We can.”
He told them, “You will drink my cup and go through my baptism. But the seats at my right and left aren’t mine to assign; they belong to those my Father has prepared them for.”
When the other ten heard about it, they were annoyed with the two brothers.
Jesus called them together and said, “You know how rulers of the nations throw their weight around, and their powerful people boss everyone.”
“It won’t be like that among you. Whoever wants to be great among you must serve the others.”
“Whoever wants to be first among you must become everyone’s slave.”
“That’s how the Son of Man came—not to be served, but to serve, and to give his life as a ransom for many.”
As they were leaving Jericho, a huge crowd followed Jesus.
Two blind men were sitting beside the road. When they heard Jesus was passing by, they shouted, “Lord, have mercy on us, Son of David!”
The crowd told them to be quiet, but they shouted even louder: “Lord, have mercy on us, Son of David!”
Jesus stopped, called them over, and asked, “What do you want me to do for you?”
They told him, “Lord, open our eyes.”
Jesus felt compassion for them and touched their eyes. Instantly they could see, and they followed him.
